name: Brittany

flag.description: Nine horizontal stripes, five black alternating with four white, and a white canton scattered with black ermine spots.
flag.symbolism: The five black stripes stand for the traditionally Gallo-speaking dioceses of Upper Brittany and the four white ones for the Breton-speaking dioceses of Lower Brittany; the ermine comes from the arms of the Duchy of Brittany.

hook: Brittany is Uruguay's nine-stripe layout in black and white, with ermine tails in the corner instead of a sun.
trivia: The Gwenn-ha-du, Breton for "white and black", was designed by Morvan Marchal in 1923; it has no official status but is flown widely, including on many town halls.
It is also flown in Loire-Atlantique, around Nantes, which belonged to historic Brittany but lies outside today's region.
